runs.entry: Price **$34.72** a share (close 2026-10-16, `tools/run.py` live quote, aggregator, flagged). Shares **256,044,428**, one class (10-Q Q3 FY2026 cover, `0000831641-26-000017`, as of 2026-07-20; checked against the balance sheet, no share-issuing filing after it; fourth-quarter repurchases not yet filed); cap **$8,889.8M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-16). Documents read: 10-K FY2025 (`0000831641-25-000032`), 10-Q Q3 FY2026, DEF 14A of 2026-01-09 (`0001104659-26-002458`), the 8-Ks of 2025-10 to 2026-09, the 10-Ks FY2019 to FY2024 for the cycle. Cross-check: FY2025 operating cash $457,685 thousand on the filed statement against 457.7 tagged. The brief's one stated departure: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 of the FY2025 10-K (eleven, listed in Step 0). Rivals from the 10-K's own list: AECOM, Jacobs and Stantec (40-F, IFRS, CAD); Booz Allen, Exponent, ICF, Leidos and SAIC named but not taken (the brief's limit of three); Arcadis, AtkinsRealis, Black & Veatch, Brown & Caldwell, CDM Smith, GHD, TRC, Weston and WSP flagged as not SEC filers. **Q1 IN**, narrowly: a labour-based engineering consultancy whose economics read from the filings; the doubt is how long the edge lasts, Q2's. **Q2 OUT** **[M2012-106]**, **[M1995-038]**, **[L2007-004]**, **[M2011-015]**: two near-equal parts, CIG 51.0% of five-year segment operating income decides, GSG read beside it; the filer's own Item 1A: "highly fragmented" markets, services that "provide limited barriers against new competitors", competition that "could force us to make price concessions"; federal costs recoverable only as the customer allows; USAID, 13.0% of FY2024 revenue, "terminated for convenience with immediate effect", federal revenue down 32.5% in the first nine months of FY2026; every client may terminate without cause. The rivals: pre-tax operating income over equity plus net debt FY2016-2025 Tetra Tech 18.9%, AECOM 10.8%, Jacobs 10.4%, Stantec 12.3%, but AECOM 26.9% and Jacobs 18.6% against Tetra Tech's 17.2% in FY2025 after AECOM sold its construction and management-services units and Jacobs separated its government units in 2024: the decade's lead matched within two years once the rivals adopted the same mix. The analyst recorded that a second analyst weighting the decade's lead could close TOO HARD on whether an execution edge lasts. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: capital spending $18.6M on $5,442.6M revenue, tangible equity below zero since FY2023 (goodwill $718M to $2,050M), receivables 27.6% to 21.3% of revenue, contract liabilities $420.3M; debt $810M at face (credit facility $235M, $575M of 2.25% convertibles due 2028-08-15) against $230.8M cash; earn-out liabilities $113.8M; buybacks at an average $34.22 (FY2025) and $31.29 (first nine months FY2026), a further $500M authorized 2026-09-10. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged**: the Hunters Point False Claims Act and CERCLA matter at subsidiary Tetra Tech EC, defended "vigorously" FY2019 to FY2023 and settled 2025-01-17 for $97M with "no admission of liability", $18M more reserved; the $115.0M charge called "non-recurring" and excluded from adjusted results; the AIP operating income ($603.6M) and cash flow ($554.7M) equal the figures excluding the charge and adding back the payments, though the plan's footnote does not name legal charges among its exclusions; a special $50,000 bonus to executives other than the CEO for "record results"; EBITDA and adjusted EPS in the release headlines, guidance given and raised. Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, capital spending and finance-lease principal) FY2021 to FY2025 $270.0M, $295.1M, $307.4M, $302.9M, $397.4M, average **$314.6M**, $335.3M on the all-equity basis; FY2025 aberrational on the filer's words (disaster-response collections, USAID collections, the $97M paid) but no cycle in the series to set a base, the five-year average kept. A serial acquirer ($1,186.2M of purchases against $786.4M, half of owner cash before purchases), so the organic pair at the filer's reported organic growth, 6.67% a year. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value range **$21.78 to $38.75** a share (all-equity, organic pair, at 5.43%; equity-only $22.63 to $38.54; the default pair $14.78 to $39.93), net debt $597.6M; the best case 5.96% at the price, no case earns the floor, so Q7 would have closed OUT; fair **$14.58 all-equity** ($15.87 equity-only); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: one name-filtered listing of `Test Runs/` for "ttek" and "tetra" before the first fetch, returning nothing (a breach, unchecked in its self-audit); the CDNL commit subjects in its opening context; recalled press reports of criminal pleas at the subsidiary, in no filing read; none used. Commits 5903fa05 (template), 8c4f6875 (Step 0 to Q1), a1b14934 (Q2), 9a3e7cdc (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS; the dispatcher's `fold_cite_check2.py`, 19 quoted fragments beside an id, all in their rows, and `fold_cite_check.py` no phantom id and no E-id (its paragraph-level flags are filing quotes and the run's own wording, read by hand): **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q2's OUT against TOO HARD for an execution edge that led for a decade and was then matched; (2) no Q2 measure for a business whose capital is its people, return on tangible assets unbounded across the field; (3) specific (a) where the end year is aberrational but owner cash shows no cycle; (4) a decline known after the window, which (b) does not reach; (5) organic growth reported in revenue, for four of five years; (6) net debt silent on earn-outs and convertibles; (7) the default pair's no-growth case spending ten years of purchase money; (8) where EBITDA in a headline lands, Q4 or Q5. Could not get: an FY2021 organic figure, an owner-cash cycle base, win or rebid rates, fourth-quarter FY2026 buybacks.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Tetra Tech, water, environment and infrastructure consulting and engineering in two near-equal segments, RPS bought for $784M in fiscal 2023, a new CEO from 2026-02-19). Q1 IN narrowly. The castle open on the filer's own words: "highly fragmented" markets with "limited barriers against new competitors", competition that can force price concessions, USAID (13.0% of FY2024 revenue) terminated for convenience; ten-year returns above AECOM, Jacobs and Stantec, but AECOM and Jacobs at or above it by FY2024-25 once they adopted the same mix; the analyst noted a TOO HARD reading was arguable. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the Hunters Point False Claims Act settlement of $97M after years of "vigorously", the charge excluded from adjusted results and from the bonus metrics, a special bonus for record results, EBITDA in the headlines. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $21.78 to $38.75 all-equity (organic pair, serial acquirer) against $34.72, no case earning the floor, fair $14.58 all-equity, $15.87 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: OUT against TOO HARD for a matched execution edge, a Q2 measure for a people business, (a) with no cycle, a decline after the window, organic growth in revenue terms, earn-outs and convertibles in net debt, EBITDA headlines between Q4 and Q5.
